title: Competing Claims for Assets Forfeited by Those Convicted in Money Laundering Case
what_it_is: Competing Claims for Assets Forfeited by Those Convicted in Money Laundering Case

sections.label: No competing claims lodged
sections.summary: No foreign governments or parties have lodged competing claims with the Courts to the forfeited assets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To date, there have not been any competing claims to the forfeited assets lodged with the Courts, by foreign governments or parties.

sections.label: Forfeited assets and foreign claims
sections.summary: Forfeited assets are with the consolidated account, and foreign jurisdictions can still request mutual legal assistance to assert claims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Yes, the forfeited assets have been placed with the consolidated account under the Accountant-General's Department.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the point as to whether or not foreign parties can still assert a claim, foreign jurisdictions can make a formal request to Singapore for mutual legal assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Through this process, they can assert a claim to seize assets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Singapore can provide mutual legal assistance to foreign jurisdictions which include sharing information in relation to the movement of the assets, the enforcement of foreign confiscation orders and we can also work together with foreign authorities on issues of assets sharing and the return of assets on a case-by-base.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Yes, there is still an open process by which foreign jurisdictions can still make a formal request to Singapore for mutual legal assistance.
